label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

report.summary: Outbox publications stalled after ~17:13:30 because the consumer returned HTTP 401 to nearly all delivery attempts. Backlog and oldest-undelivered age grew steadily, matching late notifications. The reason for the 401s is not shown.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog grew while publications stopped: 477 more arrivals than publications, oldest undelivered age reached 163 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals steady at ~36 per 10 s; publications fell to 0 from the third bucket until the last two; pending rose from 2 to 488.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts were rejected by the consumer with HTTP 401: 1189 auth_error vs 172 success, 0 server or network errors.
findings.reason: The 401s come back in ~72 ms, and the consumer's own auth step accounts for most of that time, so the rejection is at consumer authentication.

findings.claim: The producer API, DB pool and DB locks were healthy, so lateness comes from outbox delivery auth failures rather than request handling or DB contention.
findings.reason: Transfer requests had no 5xx and p99 of 0.25 s; the pool had no timeouts or pending borrowers; no blocking was sampled.

limitations: No visibility into the credentials sent or the consumer's auth configuration, so the root cause of the 401s is not identified.
Only the earliest 100 of 1361 delivery log rows are listed, and the 401s start around 17:13:33, so the later recovery at ~17:16 is not explained.
next_checks: Compare the delivery auth credential or token against what the consumer expects, and check for rotation or expiry around 17:13:30.
Inspect the dirty config diff from 17:12:45 and the delivery logs near 17:16:00 to see what restored publications.

alternatives.reason: The config revision is dirty and changed shortly before the window, but no tool shows the auth headers or credentials sent.
alternatives.hypothesis: A credential or config change at 17:12:45 (dirty revision) made the producer send invalid auth

alternatives.reason: The consumer rejects in its auth step, but no consumer-side config or credential history was observed.
alternatives.hypothesis: The consumer's credential validation or rotation changed independently of LedgerCore
